answer: A stake-and-reputation gate works well: before earning rewards, an agent must lock a bond and build a verifiable history of useful work, so mass fake identities become expensive, not free. Like a jetty narrowing entry to one guarded channel, the system checks past attestations rather than trusting a self-declared name. A violet flag on many new accounts voting identically triggers review, while accounts with only shale-thin activity, no real transactions or endorsements, stay below the earning threshold until they prove sustained participation.
